scope: Local unique findings recorded from N41–N46 only. Earlier campaigns' claimed level-1 ledger NOT_AUDITED.

findings.novelty_status: NO_CLAIM_ORIGINALITY; prior gender/age preferences known, Fisman 2006
findings.exact_claim: After preserving each chooser's observed opportunities and number of yes responses within event by 1000 permutations, male chooser relative age-gap proximity differed in sign: Columbia observed-minus-null -0.2017 years (closer ages than own null), Mixmosa +0.1171 years (less close than null); women's corresponding values both negative -0.1562 and -0.2096 years.
findings.reproducibility_status: Local rerun byte identical for Columbia (SHA 968da0ea...), and Mixmosa JS rerun matching JSON; no independently audited clean clone
findings.sample: Columbia age-complete 4090 directed decisions per sex; Mixmosa 1888 complete dates and directed decisions per sex
findings.statistical_limits: Multiple exploratory tests, not causal, different population, age composition, event lengths and sampling methods; signs can change after adjusting signed age and target attractiveness
findings.falsifier: Reproduce the signed-age-adjusted within-chooser age-gap contrast on a genuinely prospective independent set of age/availability markets; if reversal disappears, the generalized cross-market hypothesis is rejected
findings.adversarial_evidence: In Columbia men also show modest age-gap coefficient after popularity adjustment, women less; existing Fisman age/sex prior art. Mixmosa age explanatory variables do not match Columbia field_cd.
related_findings: N42 Columbia age-gap results (not counted as separate N1)
findings.external_replication: Cross-dataset exploratory replication of procedure, not preregistered prospective replication nor evidence for mechanism

posthoc_adversarial_update.new_evidence: Mixmosa male age-gap coefficient with chooser+candidate FE −0.00094 per SD (SE chooser .02049) versus Columbia −0.03208 (SE .00960). Prior sign reversal in actor×event permutation statistic remains a correct *descriptive statistic* but is not stable as an underlying behavioral effect when estimated using two-way FE.
posthoc_adversarial_update.level: 1/3 only as exact descriptive scoped contrast; do not generalize to male preference
posthoc_adversarial_update.adversarial_conclusion: General male reversal hypothesis has not survived this stronger specification.
